nodes.description: Mutant fibulin-3 alters the extracellular matrix of the RPE basal lamina and Bruch's membrane. In knock-in mice the basal deposits are made of normal ECM components in abnormal amounts and contain fibulin-3 and its binding partner TIMP3; proteoglycans accumulate in Bruch's membrane and diffusion across it is impaired. ECM turnover is altered, but the reported direction of the MMP-2 change depends on the system: knock-in Bruch's membrane shows reduced MMP-2 and MMP-9 with increased TIMP-3, whereas engineered and patient-derived RPE cultures report increased MMP-2 activity or activation.

nodes.description: Two independently generated knock-in lines carry the disease mutation in murine Efemp1. The model has been used to show that removal or inhibition of C3, factor B, Nlrp3/caspase-1 and GSK3 reduces deposits.

nodes.description: The heterozygous EFEMP1 p.Arg345Trp substitution causes fibulin-3 to misfold, in part through reduced native disulfide bonding in the domain carrying residue 345. Wild-type fibulin-3 is secreted, whereas the mutant is secreted inefficiently and retained within RPE cells. Loss of fibulin-3 does not reproduce the disease in mice, and Efemp1 knockout protects against sub-RPE deposits, so the variant acts as a toxic gain of function rather than through haploinsufficiency. Fibulin-3 is an extracellular matrix protein (its GO molecular function annotation is extracellular matrix structural constituent); that function is bound here as abnormal rather than decreased, because the mutant protein is retained and deposited abnormally rather than simply lost.

evidence.reference_title: Formation and progression of sub-retinal pigment epithelium deposits in Efemp1 mutation knock-in mice: a model for the early pathogenic course of macular degeneration.
evidence.snippet: Small, isolated sub-RPE deposits developed as early as 4 months of age in both heterozygous and homozygous knock-in mice.

evidence.reference_title: Drusen in patient-derived hiPSC-RPE models of macular dystrophies.
evidence.snippet: demonstrate that dysfunction of RPE cells alone is sufficient for the initiation of sub-RPE lipoproteinaceous deposit (drusen) formation and extracellular matrix (ECM) alteration in these diseases

evidence.reference_title: Malattia Leventinese/Doyne Honeycomb Retinal Dystrophy: Similarities to Age-Related Macular Degeneration and Potential Therapies.
evidence.snippet: The most prominent feature of ML/DHRD is the development of radial or honeycomb patterns of drusen which can develop as early as adolescence.

experimental_models.description: Forms drusen-like deposits beneath patient RPE in culture.
experimental_models.name: Patient-derived DHRD iPSC-RPE

nodes.description: Submacular hemorrhage from a neovascular membrane, an occasional presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Malattia leventinese presenting with subretinal neovascular membrane and hemorrhage.
evidence.snippet: Patients with malattia leventinese may occasionally present with submacular hemorrhage.

nodes.description: Recurrent missense variant in fibulin-3 and the only variant included in the ClinGen curation. Other EFEMP1 variants cause different phenotypes and are out of scope here.

evidence.reference_title: Widening the Spectrum of Disease Expression due to Heterozygous Variants in EFEMP1.
evidence.snippet: Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy or malattia leventinese (DHRD/ML) is an autosomal dominant retinal disorder caused by a single recurrent p.Arg345Trp (NM_001039348.3:c.1033C>T) variant in EFEMP1

evidence.reference_title: EFEMP1 / Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: Only one missense pathogenic variant (p.Arg345Trp) is included in this curation

evidence.reference_title: First reported case of Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy (Malattia Leventinese/autosomal dominant drusen) in Scandinavia.
evidence.snippet: Family history revealed no other cases of similar visual impairment suggesting a de novo mutation.
